question: What was the maximum limit of Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) that was recommended by the Narasimhan Committee?
solution:
The correct answer is __**25%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Narasimhan Committee was set up in the early 1990s to recommend reforms for the Indian banking sector.
 
• One of the key recommendations was to reduce the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) to improve the efficiency and profitability of banks.
 
• The committee recommended that the SLR be reduced to 25% of banks' net demand and time liabilities.
 
• This recommendation was aimed at freeing up funds for banks to lend to productive sectors of the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)**

 
 
• SLR is the percentage of a bank's net demand and time liabilities that must be maintained in the form of liquid assets such as cash, gold, or government-approved securities.
 
• It is a tool used by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to control the expansion of credit by the banks.
 
• Maintaining a high SLR restricts the bank's leverage in pumping more money into the economy and thus controls inflation.
 
• On the other hand, a lower SLR can boost lending and investment activities, thereby promoting economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Narasimhan Committee**
 
 
• The Narasimhan Committee was set up under the chairmanship of M. Narasimhan, a former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, in 1991.
 
• The committee's primary objective was to recommend measures to improve the efficiency and competitiveness of the Indian banking sector.
 
• Its key recommendations included reducing the SLR, deregulating interest rates, and allowing greater competition in the banking sector.
 
• The committee's recommendations have been instrumental in shaping the modern banking landscape in India.
